expectations.evidence: global-error-handler.ts: @Injectable() decorator present, class implements ErrorHandler

app.config.ts does NOT include provideBrowserGlobalErrorListeners(). Providers are provideZoneChangeDetection, provideRouter, provideHttpClient, and { provide: ErrorHandler, useClass: GlobalErrorHandler } only.

todos.component.ts JSDoc: 'resource errors are LOCAL — they surface as resource.error() signal values... They do NOT bubble up to GlobalErrorHandler automatically'. todos-with-http-resource.component.ts: 'errors are local to the resource and do NOT reach GlobalErrorHandler'. Tests in todos.component.spec.ts and todos-with-http-resource.component.spec.ts include 'does NOT propagate the HTTP error to GlobalErrorHandler' test cases.

Neither todos.component.spec.ts nor todos-with-http-resource.component.spec.ts uses rethrowApplicationErrors: false. The error isolation tests in these files use fakeAsync/tick pattern instead of rethrowApplicationErrors, which means TestBed may rethrow resource errors and fail the tests in practice.
ErrorReportingService is a Sentry-like stub with captureException() and captureMessage() methods and inline comment showing Sentry.captureException() replacement. GlobalErrorHandler delegates to it.
app.config.ts: { provide: ErrorHandler, useClass: GlobalErrorHandler } is present
GlobalErrorHandler uses inject(ErrorReportingService) via private field syntax (#errorReporting = inject(...)). TodosComponent uses inject(HttpClient). All DI via inject() function.

todos.component.ts uses rxResource (NOT httpResource/resource directly) and accesses todos.value() inside @else branch WITHOUT a .hasValue() guard — the template goes straight to @else { <ul>@for todo of todos.value()... } after checking isLoading and error. This is missing the hasValue() guard and misses the explicit resource()/httpResource() demonstration. todos-with-http-resource.component.ts is the httpResource variant but also lacks .hasValue() guard — uses @else branch instead.
